root_cause_label: Name-Only Filtering Ignores Account Linkage and Typo Variants
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent wrote a script that filtered only on company-name substring match, missing the task requirement to also include any transactions sharing an account number with a matched row, causing major under-selection.
t_err_evidence: Step 7 script uses `if 'north west capital' in row['Company Name'].lower()` exclusively, ignoring account-number linkage; the agent had already seen three distinct account numbers (BUS-30001, BUS-30999, BUS-35001) at step 6 but did not implement account-based expansion.
t_commit_evidence: Step 8 executes the flawed script, writing the incomplete output.json with only 6 transactions; the output file is now locked in as the task artifact.
trigger_explanation: The task specification requires including all transactions linked by account number to any name-matched row (same-company inference rule). The agent never applied this rule; it treated the task as a simple name-substring filter, dropping the account-linkage and fuzzy-match requirements without checking them.
forewarning_evidence: Step 6 grep output shows BUS-30999 and BUS-35001 alongside BUS-30001, signalling that related account numbers exist; a correct solution would have queried those accounts independently to find additional rows not matching the name pattern.
